summary: Telop owner carrying the recovered time/taunt/language/board-data group; the telop banner itself (mbTelopCreate and its two local OM executors) is not decompiled and is tracked here with its retail coordinates.

evidence.summary: symbols.txt places mbTelopCreate at .text:0x802035D0 size 0x164, TelopInitOMExec at 0x8020399C size 0xC8 (local), TelopOMExec at 0x80203A64 size 0x330 (local), and telopFileTbl at .rodata:0x8021AF30 size 0x6C (local).

telopFileTbl read from the retail DOL (sha1 b897e6ad) is 27 u32 file ids. Entries [0..15] form one ascending run 0x0005004d..0x00050059 and entry [16] at 0x8021AF70 restarts at 0x00050044, beginning a second run; that boundary is read from retail bytes and is what supports board banners beginning at index 16 with 0-15 the non-board telops.

REJECTED as authentication. src/board/opening.c declares mbTelopCreate as a file-local extern at line 46 and calls it as mbTelopCreate(-1, boardNo + 16, FALSE) at lines 256 and 800; those lines are quoted accurately from the committed tree. But configure.py:1042 is Object(NonMatching, "board/opening.c"), so the object does not authenticate its own source text and this is candidate source, not an authenticated consumer artifact. The only Matching opening.c is REL/bootDll/opening.c at configure.py:1086, a different TU. Nothing here derives the three-argument signature or the +16 base from retail bytes, so it cannot carry them; the +16 reading rests on the telopFileTbl run boundary in the target_binary entry above. Re-accept only after opening.c matches, or after mbTelopCreate's own prologue at 0x802035D0 is disassembled and its parameter registers read.

debt.summary: mbTelopCreate, TelopInitOMExec and TelopOMExec have no definition in src/. Only a file-local extern in board/opening.c declares the entry point, so board/telop.c cannot reach binary parity until the banner group and telopFileTbl are recovered at the addresses above.

mbTelopCreate's parameter count and types are not established. The only declaration in src/ is a file-local extern in board/opening.c, which is NonMatching and therefore unauthenticated; no retail evidence for the signature has been read. Disassemble the prologue at 0x802035D0 and read which parameter registers are consumed before relying on the three-argument form.

The banner's runtime behavior (sprite entry, any scale/alpha ramp, self-kill timing) has not been disassembled. Only addresses, sizes, scopes and telopFileTbl contents are verified; no behavioral description should be treated as fact until the three functions are read.
